name: Stored energy of the device: E = (1/2) C V^2 per capacitor and E = I * area * t for the laser

source.located: Two layers. (i) The laws: E = int V dQ = (1/2)CV^2 for a linear capacitor, and pulse energy = peak power x duration (x shape factor) -- textbook, no arXiv source is cited or needed; derived symbolically here. (ii) The parameters: Drive folder 'Warp' (id 1U2VjhhcC28qEu3NeLilwVi1k_dB6FUo7), pulsed_ignition_and_optics_specification.pdf (id 1TrZc7CBf-msA10ZW_8w4z538788pAkNJ) sect. 1.1 and 2.1, schematics_and_blueprints.pdf (id 1bugkRaEvcWdFLl888HQNcJ3jIS_5_kQA), transient_metric_propulsion_specification.pdf (id 1zv_kkVd1q3nebHMZELwdU8stInJ29tuz) sect. 4.1.

published_statement: pulsed_ignition sect. 1.1: 'High-voltage DC supply charges ten 100 nF energy storage capacitors (C_1...C_10) in parallel through 1 MOhm ceramic isolation resistors up to +50 kV DC' ... 'V_out = 10 x 50 kV = 500 kV at 10 kA peak current'; component table: 'Storage Capacitors 10x 100 nF / 60 kV'; 'Discharge Time ~12 ns Half-Width Half-Max (FWHM)'. Header: 'SUBSYSTEM B: 8-Channel Femtosecond Injection Optics PEAK POWER: 10 Petawatts (Coherent Pulse)'. Sect. 2: 'The 500 kV output pulse drives an array of eight chirped-pulse amplification (CPA) laser heads'. Sect. 2.1: 'femtosecond pulses (30 fs duration)'; 'master pulse is divided into eight equal channels'; 'focused by off-axis parabolic mirrors (f/1)'; 'diffraction-limited spot diameter of 0.1 mm (100 um) ... achieving localized intensities exceeding 10^20 W/cm^2'. Sect. 3: '[110.006 ms] Electromagnetic Shear + Optical Intensity Spikes to Planck Threshold'; '[0 ms] REBCO Stator Coils Ramp to 20 Tesla'; '[100 ms] ... Spin Central Rotor to 85,000 RPM'. Blueprints: 'Flywheel Rotor Diameter: 1.8 meters Carbon-Fiber Wrapped Beryllium-Copper Alloy'; 'Outer Shield Shell Diameter: 2.5 meters'. Transient-metric sect. 4.1: 'A central copper disc containing a muon-catalyzed fusion (muCF) starter cell'. The document itself never computes a stored energy -- the tree's 1250 J / 235.6 J / 1485.6 J are the tree's arithmetic on these parameters.
published_hypotheses: Capacitors are charged IN PARALLEL, each 'up to +50 kV' (an upper bound, not an operating point); rated 60 kV
Erected in series to 500 kV at 10 kA; discharge ~12 ns
Laser: 8 CPA channels from one 800 nm, 30 fs master pulse; subsystem PEAK POWER 10 PW; intensity 'exceeding' 1e20 W/cm^2 (a lower bound) in a 0.1 mm DIAMETER spot
The Marx pulse DRIVES the laser heads (sect. 2) -- i.e. the laser draws on the Marx store
Other energized subsystems at T+110 ms: 20 T REBCO stator, counter-rotating 1.8 m rotors at 85,000 RPM, a muon-catalysed-fusion starter cell (no mass, volume or energy given for any of them)
The Planck claim is worded as INTENSITY ('Optical Intensity Spikes to Planck Threshold'), not total energy
Law hypotheses (textbook): linear capacitor Q = CV; pulse energy = integral of power over time
hypothesis_drift: ADDED by the tree -- 'total store = Marx + laser only' (canonical hypothesis 3; warpfolder.py:287-288 stored_joules(), headline :22-23 'The device stores 1,486 J'): the source energizes a 20 T stator, two 85,000 RPM rotors and a muCF starter cell at the same moment and quantifies none of them. With the stator field and a rotor bounded by the 2.5 m envelope the ceiling is 5.4e10 J (burst-limited T1000 rotor) to 1.7e12 J (rotor held at 85k RPM, which warpfolder sect. 3 shows it cannot be) -> 8.22 to 6.73 orders short, not 15.78. The 1,486 J is the PULSED store, not the device's.

rederivation.outcome: 0 fails. Symbolic: int_0^{CV} q/C dq = CV^2/2; n(1/2)CV^2 = (1/2)(C/n)(nV)^2 (erected Marx stores the same). Numeric: 1250 J, 235.62 J, 1485.6 J, 6.050e15 = 15.7817 orders, E_P = 1.9561e9 J, 7.595e-7 all reproduced exactly. Sensitivity: every parameter reading in the document gives 15.33-15.86 orders; adding the unquantified rotor and 20 T field inside the 2.5 m envelope gives 8.22 (burst-limited) / 6.73 (held at 85k RPM) orders -- the gap would need a 5.6e11 kg rotor or a 5.6e10 m^3 (3.84 km cube) 20 T field. Planck: energy reading 7.6e-7 (laser only: 1.5e-7), intensity reading 9.2e-99, energy-density 9.2e-99, below even Schwinger (5.5e-10). Document discrepancies found (recorded, not quoted as errors of physics): 50 ohm x 10 nF = 500 ns against the stated ~12 ns discharge; f/1 at 800 nm is diffraction-limited at ~2 um, not the stated 'diffraction-limited 0.1 mm'; '12 ns Half-Width Half-Max (FWHM)' mislabels itself.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested: the external results here are two textbook energy laws (1/2 CV^2, P x t) that have no data inputs of their own beyond the linear-capacitor assumption, which film capacitors meet; there is no datum the classical authors lacked that could move them. The only data are the document's printed parameters, READ at source and all taken at the value the document prints. What the TREE lacked is not data but the rest of the document: it omitted the 10 PW figure the document prints (0.02 orders against the document), the Marx-drives-laser architecture (0.075 orders in the document's favour), and the rotor/stator/muCF stores the document names but never quantifies (up to ~9 orders in the document's favour if bounded by the 2.5 m envelope). Evidence either way: none of these, nor any reading of the Planck claim, closes the gap -- the smallest shortfall computable from any bound here is 5.4e6 (6.73 orders).
grade_evidence: The laws STAND (sympy: (1/2)CV^2 and its erection invariance; P x t) and the tree's arithmetic is reproduced to every printed digit, so on the tree's own hypothesis 'store = Marx + laser' the figures are right. But that hypothesis is ADDED by the tree: the source energizes a 20 T stator, 85,000 RPM rotors and a muCF starter cell and quantifies none, so '1,486 J stored' and '15.78 orders' hold for the PULSED store only; bounded by the 2.5 m envelope the device's shortfall is >= 6.73 orders (8.22 with a rotor at its burst limit). The conclusions that rest on it -- ENERGY_BUDGET_IS_CONNECTED_TO_THE_CHAIN = False, REACHES_PLANCK_THRESHOLD = False, S9 REFUSED -- survive every reading computed. Two further tree choices are in the document's favour (laser double-counted with the Marx that drives it; whole-store energy compared with E_P where the document says intensity, 9.2e-99), and one is against it by 0.02 orders (1e20 lower bound used instead of the printed 10 PW). Not WRONG: no computed contradiction of any tree conclusion; the moved figure is a hypothesis scope, not a refutation.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: warpfolder.py's statement restricted to 'the pulsed store (Marx + laser) is 1,486 J, 15.78 orders short', with the rotor/stator/muCF named as unquantified stores bounded at >= 6.7 orders short -- i.e. the hypothesis the tree adds made explicit. To WRONG: a reading of the documents that supplies a store >= 8.99e18 J (none exists: it needs a 5.6e11 kg rotor at 85k RPM or a 3.84 km cube of 20 T field) -- or a document parameter misread (checked: 50 kV per stage in parallel, 0.1 mm diameter, 30 fs, all as READ). To DATA-DEPENDENT: the folder publishing a rotor mass or field volume that moves the conclusion -- the envelope bound says no such value fits in 2.5 m.
